route: degenerate -- Degenerate one-player games: ties as a resource, and a run longer than the Holt-Klee ceiling with one player
headline: Task (1) is answered NEGATIVELY and completely: no one-player stopping SSG with |Vmax|=4 has an all-switches run of length 7, degenerate or not, so h*_1(4) = h*_HK(4) = 6 and the crack rem:oneplayer-lp left open is closed at m=4. Task (2) is answered by a SHARP theorem in the wrong direction for the route: a zero-tie timer runs for at most |Vmax| rounds and the bound is attained by an explicit staircase, so the timer mechanism is provably linear and cannot yield the superlinear family of task (3). Task (4): h*_deg1(m) = 1,2,4,6 for m <= 4, attained by degenerate games for m >= 2; non-Holt-Klee corner resolutions DO arise, so what survives degeneracy is the bound on the run, not Holt-Klee for resolutions.

results.name: degen:prop-partial-lp
results.statement: For EVERY stopping one-player SSG (degenerate or not) with |Vmax| = m: the d'Epenoux occupancy polytope X(G) has exactly the 2^m vertices y^sigma >= 1, is a simple m-polytope whose graph is the m-cube and whose faces are its subcubes, obj(y^sigma) = sum_v val_sigma(v), and obj(y^{sigma[v]}) - obj(y^sigma) is >0 / =0 / <0 according as v in S_sigma / v in D_sigma / neither. Hence the flat classes of def:flat are exactly the faces of X(G) on which obj is constant, and the partial improvement structure (S,D) is the partial orientation induced by obj on the graph of X(G).
results.argument: prop:oneplayer-lp's proof of the polytope combinatorics never uses nondegeneracy (it enters only in its last paragraph, about edges). The three-case sign law is lem:switch for v in S, lem:trichotomy(c) for v in D, and lem:trichotomy(b) applied at sigma[v] otherwise, summed over vertices. The last sentence is lem:flat-class(a) plus 'faces are subcubes'.
results.verification: t_op.py: the outmap, the identity obj(y^sigma) = sum val_sigma and the sign law recomputed in exact rationals on 13 of the solo round's one-player realisations (12 AP games at m=4 of height 6, one at m=3 of height 4). sweep.py: 0 sign-law violations and 0 flat-class violations over 580 random one-player games at m=4,5,6 (all 2^m strategies each).

results.name: degen:lem-perturb
results.statement: Let G be one-player stopping with run sigma_0..sigma_L, d a linear functional on R^{2m} and d' a linear functional non-constant on every edge of X(G) on which obj and d are both constant. For small eps>0 the functional c = obj + eps d + eps^2 d' is generic on X(G), so its orientation s_eps is an AUSO of the m-cube satisfying Holt-Klee on every face, with S(sigma) subset s_eps(sigma) subset S(sigma) u D(sigma). If moreover (*) d(y^{sigma_t}) > d(y^{sigma_t[v]}) for every t and every v in D(sigma_t), then s_eps(sigma_t) = S(sigma_t) for all t, the run is the bottom-antipodal walk of s_eps from sigma_0, and L <= h*_HK(m).
results.argument: Finitely many edges, so a single eps makes the sign of Delta c lexicographic in (obj, d, d'). The orientation of a polytope graph by a generic linear functional has a unique sink on every face and is acyclic, and Holt-Klee's theorem gives dim(F) internally vertex-disjoint monotone paths on each face F; the faces of X(G) are the subcubes by degen:prop-partial-lp. (Holt-Klee, and Gaertner-Morris-Ruest for realisable USOs, cited from memory, unchecked against the source, exactly as rem:oneplayer-lp already does.)
results.verification: The construction is used and its conclusion checked on every instance below; the Holt-Klee test itself (unit vertex-capacity max flow on every face, cube.py) reproduces the solo round's census flags on all 144 AUSO classes of the 4-cube of height >= 6 and gives h*_HK(4) = 6 (t_census.py, t_all.py step 1).

results.name: degen:lem-gperturb
results.statement: Stronger form: perturb the GAME, not just the objective. With harmonic normal form (p,q), every row leaking to t0, call (pi,rho) admissible if pi^{v,a}_w >= 0 wherever p^{v,a}_w = 0 and rho_{v,a} >= 0 wherever q^{v,a} = 0; put u_sigma = (I-P_sigma)^{-1}(pi_sigma val_sigma + rho_sigma) and Delta(sigma,v) = rho_{v,abar} - rho_{v,a} + (pi^{v,abar} - pi^{v,a}).val_sigma + (p^{v,abar} - p^{v,a}).u_sigma. If some admissible (pi,rho) has (**) Delta(sigma_t,v) < 0 at every flat incidence on the run, then for a generic admissible (pi',rho') and small rational delta, eps the game with rows (p + eps(pi + delta pi'), q + eps(rho + delta rho')) is a NONDEGENERATE one-player stopping SSG with the same all-switches run, so L <= h*_HK(m) by prop:oneplayer-lp. Condition (*) is the case pi = 0 of (**).
results.argument: Each incidence's gap is a rational function of eps regular at 0; non-flat gaps keep their sign, flat gaps take the sign of the first-order term, which is Delta_{(pi,rho)} + delta Delta_{(pi',rho')}, nonzero for all small delta and of the sign of Delta_{(pi,rho)} where that is nonzero. The pi = 0 identification uses <rho, y^sigma> = sum_w u_sigma(w) together with the linear-algebra computation of thm:impedance, which is valid for an arbitrary (possibly signed) reward vector.
results.verification: gpert.py builds the 2m(m+1)-variable linear system exactly (one exact linear solve per basis direction per incidence) and decides it with the exact simplex mylp.py. On degen:prop-nolin, where (*) is infeasible, (**) IS feasible (t_gpert.py). sweep2.py: (**) tested on all 4320 runs of 191 random degenerate games at m=4,5, never infeasible.

results.name: degen:cor-onetie
results.statement: If all the flat incidences on the run occur at a single Max vertex x and all with the same action a -- in particular if the run has at most one flat incidence in total -- then (*) holds and L <= h*_HK(m).
results.argument: Take d(y) = y_{x,a}. Then d(y^{sigma_t}) = y^{sigma_t}_x >= 1 by degen:prop-partial-lp(a) while y^{sigma_t[x]} vanishes on the coordinate (x,a), so d(y^{sigma_t[x]}) = 0. There are no cross terms because only one coordinate of d is nonzero.
results.verification: Used in degen:thm-no-seven and degen:prop-five; the occupancy vectors are computed exactly (op.py y()) and the inequality is immediate from the disjoint supports.

results.name: degen:lem-seven-flat
results.statement: Take any of the 384 outmaps s of bottom-antipodal height 7 of the 4-cube and any start sigma_0 whose BA walk has length 7 (768 such pairs). Consider partitions of the 4-cube into subcubes with (F1) s(sigma) xor s(sigma') = sigma xor sigma' inside a block, (F2) s(sigma_t) & D_{A(sigma_t)} = empty at every walk vertex, (F3) the quotient digraph on blocks acyclic, (F4) lem:face-sink's sink condition. Exactly 384 of the 768 pairs -- one start per outmap -- admit a partition with a block of dimension >= 1; in every one of those the partition is unique and is the SINGLE EDGE {sigma_0, sigma_0 xor e_x} at the START, all other blocks singletons.
results.argument: Exhaustive finite computation. Each height-7 outmap has exactly four (F1)-subcubes of dimension >= 1, all edges, pairwise disjoint, so only 16 candidate partitions per pair; (F2)-(F4) and the run-length-7 requirement are then checked directly. For the representative s = (0,1,3,6,7,4,13,10,14,15,9,12,11,8,5,2) with sigma_0 = 8 (walk 8,6,11,7,13,5,1,0) the four (F1)-edges are {0,1},{6,14},{7,15},{8,9}: the first has both 0 and 1 on the walk (impossible, lem:flat-class(c)); the second and third fail (F2) because 3 in s(6)=13 and 3 in s(7)=10; the fourth survives with corner 8. The other length-7 start is 9, for which {8,9} fails (F2) since 0 in s(9)=15, leaving nothing.
results.verification: flatstruct.py + t_all.py step 2, run over the full orbit (384 outmaps generated by the 384 cube automorphisms; the orbit is free, and the census file classes4.txt independently confirms there is exactly ONE AUSO class of height 7 at m=4 and that its representative lies in this orbit).

results.name: degen:thm-no-seven
results.statement: THE ANSWER TO TASK (1), NEGATIVE. No stopping SSG with Vmin empty and |Vmax| = 4 has an all-switches run of length 7. Consequently cor:seven-two-player holds without its nondegeneracy hypothesis: the two Min vertices of G# are necessary for any game realising the height-seven orbit as a run.
results.argument: Suppose G is such a game. The run vertices lie in pairwise distinct flat classes (lem:flat-class(c)), so c_{A(sigma_t)} := sigma_t is a consistent corner choice; the resolution s' of thm:flat-resolution then has the run as its BA walk from sigma_0 (cor:ceiling-general), so height(s') >= 7 = h*(4), hence = 7, hence s' is in the unique free orbit of 384 outmaps (prop:auso-census). G's flat partition satisfies (F1)-(F4) with respect to s' -- (F1) since s'(sigma) = S_A u (sigma xor c_A), (F2) since s'(sigma_t) = S_{A(sigma_t)}, (F3) by lem:flat-class(c), (F4) by lem:face-sink. If G is nondegenerate use d = 0; otherwise degen:lem-seven-flat forces exactly one nontrivial class, the edge {sigma_0, sigma_0 xor e_x}, so the run carries exactly ONE flat incidence, at the start. Put a = sigma_0(x), d(y) = y_{x,a}: by degen:cor-onetie and degen:lem-perturb the generic functional obj + eps d + eps^2 d' induces exactly s' on X(G), so s' is an LP orientation and therefore Holt-Klee. But no height-7 outmap of the 4-cube is Holt-Klee (h*_HK(4) = 6). Contradiction.
results.verification: The only computational ingredients are degen:lem-seven-flat (exhaustive, t_all.py step 2) and h*_HK(4) = 6 with a unique height-7 class (census reread and every height >= 6 class rechecked with my own max-flow Holt-Klee test, t_census.py / t_all.py step 1). The perturbation step is pure argument; y^{sigma_0}_x >= 1 > 0 = y^{sigma_0[x]}_{(x,a)} because the two occupancy vertices have disjoint support on the coordinate (x,a).

results.name: degen:cor-hstar-one
results.statement: TASK (4). Writing h*_1(m) for the greatest all-switches run length of a stopping one-player SSG with m Max vertices: h*_1(m) = h*_HK(m) = 1, 2, 4, 6 for m = 1,2,3,4, against h*(m) = 1,2,4,7; and for m = 2,3,4 the value is already attained by a DEGENERATE game. So no law is lost and none is gained: Holt-Klee survives degeneracy as a ceiling on the run, and the height-7 class of prop:auso-census is the only class of the 4-cube that one player cannot reach.
results.argument: Upper bounds: h*_HK = h* for m <= 3 so cor:ceiling-general suffices; m = 4 is degen:thm-no-seven. Lower bounds: staircase T_m for m = 1,2; for m = 3,4 the solo round's nondegenerate realisations (B_1 game at m=3, height 4; AP games at m=4, height 6), made degenerate by retuning ONE non-chosen action's t1-mass so that a single incidence ties, with the run unchanged.
results.verification: t_deg3.py, t_deg6.py, exact: m=3 degenerate game with run 6->3->5->1->0 (length 4) whose flat class {4,6} sits ON the run (saved deg_m3_run4.json); m=4 degenerate game with run 0->15->8->13->1->5->4 (length 6) and flat class {10,11} off the run (saved deg_m4_run6.json). Both stopping, exact rationals.

results.name: degen:prop-five
results.statement: The same at m=5 for the one height-12 class we can name. For the height-12 outmap s12 = (15,0,1,2,27,30,12,29,19,26,8,25,22,21,20,23,31,18,28,17,3,6,24,5,7,14,16,13,10,9,4,11) of prop:hstar-five (non-Holt-Klee, verified): the only starts of BA length 12 are 0 and 16, and the only (F1)-(F4) partition with a nontrivial block is the single edge {0,16} at the start 0. Hence no one-player stopping SSG with |Vmax| = 5, degenerate or not, has an all-switches run whose resolution lies in the orbit of s12.
results.argument: Identical to degen:thm-no-seven: one flat incidence on the run, so degen:cor-onetie gives a Holt-Klee LP orientation equal to the resolution, contradicting that s12 is not Holt-Klee.
results.verification: t_five.py / t_all.py step 3: s12 is a USO, acyclic, of height 12, not Holt-Klee; its (F1)-subcubes of dimension >= 1 are the seven edges {12,14},{1,3},{13,15},{29,31},{18,22},{0,16},{14,30}; 96 candidate partitions tested, exactly one survives. NOTE this does NOT give h*_1(5) <= 11: other height-12 classes of the 5-cube exist and cannot be enumerated (prop:auso-size), and h*_HK(5) = 11 is itself only measured.

results.name: degen:prop-nolin
results.statement: The hypothesis (*) is NOT automatic. The explicit one-player stopping SSG with m=4 and rows (p;q) -- x1: (0,11/16,1/4,0;0) and (0,0,1/8,0;1/8); x2: (0,5/16,0,9/16;0) and (0,0,1/4,11/16;0); x3: (5/16,0,3/16,0;0) and (0,9/16,0,1/16;0); x4: (0,0,0,0;0) and (5/8,3/16,0,0;1/16) -- is stopping (34 vertices, 28 average, every row leaks to t0); its all-switches run from sigma_0 = 7 is 7 -> 11 -> 13 and carries exactly two flat incidences, both at the Max vertex x2, at sigma=7 with action 1 and at sigma=13 with action 0. In exact arithmetic y^15 - y^13 = (61360/43111)(y^7 - y^5), so the two required inequalities d(y^7 - y^5) > 0 and d(y^13 - y^15) > 0 are contradictory: NO linear functional satisfies (*). Nevertheless the run has 24 AUSO completions of its partial orientation, 17 of them Holt-Klee, and (**) of degen:lem-gperturb is feasible, so L <= h*_HK(4) still holds here.
results.argument: Gordan's alternative: (*) fails iff some nonnegative combination of the vectors y^{sigma_t} - y^{sigma_t[v]} vanishes; the smallest way is two flat incidences at the SAME Max vertex with OPPOSITE actions, on two parallel edges of a 2-face of X(G) that is a trapezoid, which is exactly what happens here.
results.verification: t_infeas.py, t_infeas2.py: the game rebuilt standalone, S = (9,10,9,8,9,12,9,12,5,4,7,6,1,0,1,0), D = (6,0,6,0,6,2,6,2,0,0,0,0,2,2,2,2), the run recomputed FROM THE EXPLICIT GAME by exact elimination, the exact proportionality constant, and the enumeration of all 2^7 orientations of the seven flat edges with unique-sink / acyclicity / Holt-Klee tests. t_gpert.py: (**) feasible.

results.name: degen:prop-res-nonhk
results.statement: Corner resolutions (thm:flat-resolution) of DEGENERATE one-player stopping games genuinely fail Holt-Klee, confirming rem:oneplayer-lp concretely. Over 236 random degenerate m=4 instances, 3924 of 17388 corner resolutions failed the unit-capacity max-flow test; in a second, fresh sample of 116 instances, 1728 of 7450 failed, of bottom-antipodal heights 2, 3 and 4.
results.argument: Enumerate all corner choices per flat class and test each resolution. This is why degen:thm-no-seven cannot be obtained by resolving: degen:lem-perturb produces a DIFFERENT completion, orienting each flat class by a linear functional rather than towards a corner, agreeing with the corner resolution exactly where the run needs it.
results.verification: t_res.py, t_res2.py, exact values, Holt-Klee by max flow.

results.name: degen:thm-timer
results.statement: TASK (2), SHARP AND NEGATIVE FOR THE ROUTE. Let G be a stopping one-player SSG with |Vmax| = m, let sigma_0, sigma_1, ... be an all-switches run, let u be any vertex with val_{sigma_0}(u) = 0, and let T be least with val_{sigma_T}(u) > 0. Then there are Max vertices v_1,...,v_T such that the FIRST switch of v_j occurs at round T-j. They are pairwise distinct, so T <= m: a zero-tie timer cannot outlast the number of Max vertices.
results.argument: val_{sigma_t} is nondecreasing (lem:switch) and val_sigma(u) = 0 iff t1 is unreachable from u in G_sigma (lem:trap); call such u dead. CLAIM: if w is dead at sigma_{s-1} and alive at sigma_s then there is a Max vertex v, dead at sigma_{s-1}, with v in S_{s-1} being v's FIRST switch, and the target w' of v's other action dead at sigma_{s-2} and alive at sigma_{s-1}. Proof: on a sigma_s-path w = p_0 -> ... -> p_k = t1 take the largest j with p_j dead at sigma_{s-1}; then p_{j+1} is alive and the edge p_j -> p_{j+1} is absent from G_{sigma_{s-1}}, so p_j =: v is a Max vertex in S_{s-1}. It cannot have switched earlier: a switch at round t < s-1 replaces a dead chosen action by one of strictly larger value, so val_{sigma_{t+1}}(v) > 0, contradicting deadness at sigma_{s-1}. And w' cannot be alive at sigma_{s-2}, else v would already have been strictly switchable at round s-2. Iterating the claim from (u, T) down to s = 1 yields v_1,...,v_T with pairwise distinct first-switch rounds T-1, ..., 0.
results.verification: t_timer.py and sweep.py: 18833 wake-up events over 1010 random one-player games at m = 4,5,6, in exact arithmetic; max wake round exactly m at m = 4 and 5; zero violations of either T <= m or the distinct-witness structure.

results.name: degen:prop-staircase
results.statement: The bound of degen:thm-timer is sharp for every m. Let T_k be the one-player SSG with Vmax = {x_1,...,x_k}, x_1 -> (t0, t1) and x_j -> (t0, x_{j-1}) for j >= 2, and no average vertices. It is stopping, N = k+2, a = 0; from the all-first-actions start the all-switches run has length exactly k, switching {x_1},{x_2},...,{x_k} in that order, and at round t the vertices x_{t+2},...,x_k are all tied at 0. So val_{sigma_t}(x_k) = 0 for t < k and = 1 at sigma_k: a zero-tie timer of length T = k = m.
results.argument: No nonempty trap exists (the Vmax-digraph is a path into sinks), so G is stopping by lem:trapchar. Induction: after t rounds val(x_i) = 1 for i <= t and 0 for i > t, so x_{t+1} is strictly switchable and every x_j with j > t+1 has both options valued 0, hence is tied.
results.verification: t_all.py step 4, FROM THE GAME at k = 1,2,4,8,16,24: stopping by the trap test, val_sigma by exact elimination at every strategy of the run, one vertex switched per round, wake round T = k exactly. (The leaky variant with 1/2 to t0 on each second action, a = k average vertices and val(x_k) = 2^{-k}, behaves identically.)

results.name: degen:cor-gate
results.statement: TASK (3), NEGATIVE FOR THE MECHANISM. In a chain B_1 |> B_2 |> ... |> B_r in which the only routes from B_{i+1} to t1 pass through B_i (so B_{i+1} is dead until a vertex of B_i wakes), a block's vertices never switch while dead, and no vertex of B_1..B_{r-1} switches after B_r wakes, the all-switches run has length at most (m - m_r) + h*_1(m_r) <= m + max_{k <= m_r}(h*_1(k) - k), which is m + 2 for blocks with m_i <= 4. No amount of chaining raises the run length above m + O(1).
results.argument: By degen:thm-timer the wake round T of B_r has T distinct Max-vertex witnesses whose first switches are at rounds T-1,...,0; none lies in B_r, whose vertices are dead and (by hypothesis) do not switch before T. So T <= m - m_r. After round T only B_r moves, so the rest is an all-switches run of the subgame freezing the other Max vertices (def:subcube, lem:subgame(b)), whose frozen vertices have coinciding out-edges and may be retyped as average vertices; that game has m_r Max vertices, so at most h*_1(m_r) further rounds. h*_1(k) - k = 0,0,1,2 for k <= 4 by degen:cor-hstar-one.
results.verification: Consistent with the measured family below (L = m + 2 exactly at five sizes), and with the timer measurements.

results.name: degen:prop-family
results.statement: The gated family and its growth law, measured at five sizes. Let B be the nondegenerate one-player height-6 block AP_m4_k0_den1024_s1 (run 0->15->8->13->1->5->4) and let F_s place the staircase T_s beside B, routing every t1-mass of B's rows to x_s. Then F_s is a one-player stopping SSG with m = s+4, N = 2m+115, a = m+113, whose all-switches run from the all-first-actions start has length L = s+6 = m+2, carrying 4s + binom(s,2) flat incidences. Measured (s; m; N; a; L; ties on the run): (0; 4; 123; 117; 6; 0), (4; 8; 131; 121; 10; 22), (8; 12; 139; 125; 14; 60), (12; 16; 147; 129; 18; 114), (16; 20; 155; 133; 22; 184). Growth law L = m + 2, LINEAR, and by degen:cor-gate optimal for a zero-tie chain of blocks with m_i <= 4.
results.argument: B's rows do not mention the staircase, so the staircase runs as in degen:prop-staircase and theta_t = val_{sigma_t}(x_s) is 0 for t < s and 2^{-s} afterwards. The block's values solve z = P^B z + q^B theta, so z = theta val^B and every block comparison is B's multiplied by theta: for t < s all four block incidences are tied at 0 (nothing strictly switchable), and from round s on the block's strictly switchable set is exactly B's at the same strategy, so it starts at its own sigma^0 and takes 6 further rounds. Tie count sum_{t<s}(4 + (s-1-t)) = 4s + binom(s,2).
results.verification: t_all.py step 5 and t_fam3.py, FROM THE EXPLICIT FAIR-COIN GAME at all five sizes: stopping by mycore's trap test, val_sigma by exact elimination at each strategy of the run, run identical to the normal-form computation, tie counts matching the closed formula. t_famd.py additionally checks that (*) is feasible on these runs even though they carry flat classes of dimension up to 9.

gap: The general bound for one player is NOT proved. GAP, exactly: "Every stopping SSG with Vmin empty and |Vmax| = m has all-switches runs of length at most h*_HK(m); equivalently, every such run is the bottom-antipodal walk of some Holt-Klee acyclic unique sink orientation of the m-cube." What is proved instead is the sufficient condition (**) of degen:lem-gperturb (an explicit exact LP in 2m(m+1) variables, feasible on every one of the 4320 runs tested and on the family), and unconditionally the two instances where the extremal orientation forces at most one flat incidence on the run (m=4 height 7; the named m=5 height-12 class). degen:prop-nolin shows the weaker condition (*) genuinely fails on some runs, so a general proof must either complete the partial orientation non-linearly or bound the run without a perturbation. A second, smaller gap: h*_1(5) is not determined, because the height-12 classes of the 5-cube cannot be enumerated and h*_HK(5) = 11 is only a measurement (round 14's deg:prop-hk5). Two cross-references in the LaTeX are to round-14 UNINTEGRATED labels (deg:prop-zeroties, deg:prop-hk5) and will need renaming or restating by the integrator.
next_steps: 1. The route's own conclusion is that ties are not the crack: at m=4 the Holt-Klee ceiling survives degeneracy exactly, and the zero-tie timer is capped at |Vmax| rounds. Any future one-player lower-bound family must therefore beat h*_HK, not h*, and must NOT be built out of zero-tie gating. 2. The right next target is the general statement in the gap: prove L <= h*_HK(m) for all one-player games, or find a run on which (**) is infeasible. The Gordan certificate of degen:prop-nolin (two flat incidences at the same Max vertex with opposite actions, on parallel edges of a trapezoidal 2-face of X(G)) is the exact shape to engineer, and engineering it -- not sampling -- is the way, since random search over 1200+ games produced only that one (*)-failure and no (**)-failure. 3. The pivot's one-player half is now sharply posed: is h*_HK(m) superlinear, and are its maximisers realisable by one-player games? The data are h*_HK = 1,2,4,6,11 (the last measured); the solo round's blowhk.py found no HK-preserving blow-up that doubles (best 4,9,12). A one-player family of superlinear run length would be new even for Howard's rule with two actions (Mukherjee-Kalyanakrishnan's linear bound, from memory), and by degen:cor-hstar-one it must be an HK family. 4. A cheap concrete item: realise a Holt-Klee height-11 AUSO of the 5-cube by a one-player game (the solo round's realiseAP machinery plus the retuning trick of t_deg6.py); chaining such blocks by the nondegenerate threshold sequencer (values affine in a gate value theta, thresholds between consecutive theta_t -- NOT the zero-tie gate, which degen:cor-gate caps) would give L = 2.2m, against the m + 2 achieved here. 5.
